title: Formalise CharacterRecipe as a sharable JSON schema + serializer + URL/probe surfaces
intent: After S102+S103 the bench produces visibly-distinct bombers, but the recipe driving them lives in `bench-state.ts` as a module-scoped mutable object — never serialised to JSON, never validated against a schema, never readable by anything outside the bench. This blocks every downstream consumer: kaboom-crew migration can't accept 'spawn this bomber', multiplayer can't sync recipes across clients, cosmetic unlocks can't persist accessory choices, agent probes can't pin specific bomber appearances for screenshot tests. This story formalises CharacterRecipe as a real JSON schema with a serializer (recipe → base64 URL-safe string), deserializer (URL-safe string → validated recipe), a seed-only resolver (raw seed → fully-populated recipe via deterministic defaults), and exposes both as URL params + agent probes. No new generator behaviour — purely makes the existing recipe interchangeable.
rationale: Source: `docs/game-design/characters-and-visual.md` §2.1 — the recipe shape was always meant to be 'easy to serialize'. S102+S103 grew the recipe surface organically inside `bench-state.ts`; that's fine for iteration but it's never been pinned to a schema, so any consumer that wants to accept a 'bomber recipe' from outside has nothing to validate against. Blocking for GDP-2026-05-22-002 (kaboom migration — needs a serializable recipe to round-trip URL → entity). Blocking for the multiplayer recipe sync once GDP-2026-05-20-007 (network) lands. Blocking for future cosmetic-unlock persistence (unlocks store recipe diffs in a profile). Sized as a single sprint story because the schema + validator + serializer are mechanical work over an already-stable surface — no new generator code.
acceptanceHints: examples/procbomber-bench/schemas/scene-extensions.schema.json: gains a `characterRecipeDefinition` schema with every field from `docs/game-design/characters-and-visual.md` §2.1 — proportions (9 numeric scalars, S103 split), posture (3 numeric scalars), mounts (4 numeric scalars), shapes (3 enums), palette (either an 8-channel object OR a family-name string), accessories (string-enum array length 0..3), seed (u32), archetype (enum, default 'humanoid'). Schema validates exact ranges + enum sets matching what `bench-state.ts` accepts today.

examples/procbomber-bench/src/characters/recipe.ts (new file — promoted out of bench-state): `validateCharacterRecipe(input: unknown): CharacterRecipe` (throws with field-path on rejection), `resolveCharacterRecipe(seed: number, overrides?: Partial<CharacterRecipe>): CharacterRecipe` (seed → fully-populated recipe by deterministic defaults; overrides win field-by-field), `serializeCharacterRecipe(r: CharacterRecipe): string` (compact JSON, base64url, NOT base64 — must round-trip in URL without escaping), `deserializeCharacterRecipe(s: string): CharacterRecipe` (parses + validates).

Schema validator is strict on rejection: unknown fields error, out-of-range numbers error, unknown enum values error (palette family name AND accessory enum). Errors carry field path + offending value: `CharacterRecipe.proportions.headSize: 0.9 outside [0.25..0.45]`.

Deterministic default derivation: a recipe with only `{ seed: 42 }` resolves to the SAME populated recipe on every call. Test 200 random seeds, assert the resolved recipe is field-wise stable across two resolves.

Partial overrides: `resolveCharacterRecipe(42, { palette: 'ember', accessories: ['antennae'] })` returns the seed-42 default recipe with ONLY palette + accessories overridden — all other fields seed-derived. Tested.
URL surfaces (debug + agent only — NOT advertised in UI per characters-and-visual.md §6.2):
?recipe=<base64url>  — applied to the bench's bomber. Bench reads on attach + when the slider for 'paste recipe' is used.

Bench UI: a new 'Recipe' panel with two text-area widgets — 'Current recipe (JSON, read-only)' showing the serialised recipe + a 'Paste recipe to apply' input. Round-trip path is the user-facing test that the format is stable.

Bench bootstrap: replace the ad-hoc bench-state initialisation with `resolveCharacterRecipe(urlSeed ?? defaultSeed, urlRecipeOverride)`. The bench's existing slider writes become recipe-field writes (i.e. `recipe.proportions.headSize = sliderValue` instead of `benchState.headSize = sliderValue`). Internal plumbing change; UI behaviour unchanged.

Agent probe surface (new — lives in examples/procbomber-bench/bootstrap.ts, exported on window.__agf.procbomber namespace): `getRecipe(): CharacterRecipe`, `setRecipe(recipe: CharacterRecipe): void`, `setRecipeFromSeed(seed: number): void`, `resolveRecipe(seed: number): CharacterRecipe` (returns without applying — useful for previews). All four functions also accept their input via partial recipe + validate. Same surface ports to `window.__agf.kaboom.*` when GDP-2026-05-22-002 (migration) lands.

Determinism roundtrip test: random recipe → serialise → deserialise → field-wise equality. Cover all 25+ fields. Add a fuzz harness that picks random valid recipes (200 iterations) and asserts the roundtrip.

Forward compatibility hook: include a `agfFormatVersion: 1` field in serialised recipes — when version mismatches at deserialise time, throw a clear error rather than silently mangling fields. Recipe-migration story is deferred (see characters-and-visual.md §7.3 — only solve migration when v2 schema ships).

Existing bench tests stay green. The bench-state.ts module-scope object can either go away or shrink to a thin wrapper over the recipe — dev's call. The recipe.ts module is the new home for serialisation logic.

Out of scope (explicit): server-side validation in the network reference server (waits for GDP-007 multiplayer), persistent profile storage (waits for cosmetic-unlocks infra), schema-driven docs generation, GraphQL/protobuf representations of the recipe. JSON + base64url is the only encoding this story commits to.
